passage.title: Primera visita a la oficina
target: Elena Vargas es contadora en un despacho pequeño de la ciudad.
Hoy recibe a un cliente nuevo, Ramón Ortiz, que tiene una panadería.
Elena: Soy contadora y me encargo de la contabilidad de los negocios pequeños.
Ramón: ¿Usted revisa también los impuestos del negocio?
Elena: Sí, preparo las declaraciones y reviso cada documento del mes.
Ramón: Perfecto. ¿Podemos fijar una cita la próxima semana?
Elena: Claro, hoy le envío la confirmación por correo y le recuerdo qué documentos del banco debe traer.
native: Elena Vargas is an accountant at a small office in the city.
Today she receives a new client, Ramón Ortiz, who owns a bakery.
Elena: I am an accountant and I handle the bookkeeping for small businesses.
Ramón: Do you also review the business taxes?
Elena: Yes, I prepare the returns and review every document from the month.
Ramón: Perfect. Can we set an appointment for next week?
Elena: Of course, today I will send you the confirmation by email and remind you which bank documents to bring.

words.note: The feminine form of contador. Many Spanish-speaking countries use it for a professional who keeps and reports financial records.
Refers to the whole system of recording money. Use llevar la contabilidad for keeping the books.
Use for the person or business that hires you. Its plural is clientes and it does not change for gender.
A professional office, as in despacho contable. Common in Spain and Mexico; oficina or estudio are also used.
A paper or digital record. Plural documentos.
Plural in ordinary speech. The specific tax (renta, IVA) depends on the jurisdiction.
A fixed time to meet. Pedir cita means to request an appointment.
A financial institution where a business keeps its accounts.
A piece of work a professional provides for a fee.
A firm that handles accounts, payroll and tax filings for businesses. Common in Spain and some Latin American countries.

words.es: Soy contadora y trabajo con pequeños negocios.
words.en: I am an accountant and I work with small businesses.

words.note: Me encargo de means I take responsibility for a task.
Fixed polite formula with usted. ¿En qué puedo ayudarlo? or ayudarla is also correct.

words.en: Do you also review the taxes?

example.target: Trabajo con pequeños negocios.
example.native: I work with small businesses.

verbs.note: The -ar verb. With yo the ending is -o; with usted and él or ella it is -a; with ellos or ustedes it is -an.

example.target: Ayudo a mis clientes con los impuestos.
example.native: I help my clients with their taxes.

verbs.note: Ayudar takes a direct object: la ayudo, lo ayudo, los ayudo. Le ayudo is also heard, especially with usted. Con introduces the task.

example.target: Preparo las declaraciones de cada mes.
example.native: I prepare the returns each month.

verbs.note: Regular -ar pattern. Preparar takes a direct object (las declaraciones), so no preposition is needed.

example.target: Reviso los documentos antes de firmar.
example.native: I review the documents before signing.

verbs.note: Antes de plus an infinitive means before doing something: antes de firmar means before signing. The infinitive does not change.

passage.title: Confirmar la reunión
target: La asistente de Elena llama a Ramón para confirmar la reunión del martes.
Asistente: Le confirmo la cita del martes a las diez de la mañana con la contadora.
Ramón: ¿Podemos hacer la reunión por videollamada en vez de ir a la oficina?
Asistente: Sí. En ese caso, envíe los documentos al correo de la oficina antes del lunes.
Ramón: De acuerdo. ¿Qué documentos necesita la contadora?
Asistente: Los recibos de marzo y el extracto bancario de este mes.
Asistente: ¿Su correo electrónico y su dirección siguen siendo los de su última factura?
Ramón: El correo, sí; la dirección cambió y ahora es calle Mayor 12.
Asistente: Perfecto, actualizo sus datos, le envío el enlace y nos vemos el martes a las diez.
native: Elena's assistant calls Ramón to confirm Tuesday's meeting.
Assistant: I am confirming your Tuesday appointment with the accountant at ten in the morning.
Ramón: Can we hold the meeting by video call instead of going to the office?
Assistant: Yes. In that case, send the documents to the office email before Monday.
Ramón: All right. Which documents does the accountant need?
Assistant: The March receipts and this month's bank statement.
Assistant: Are your email and your address still the ones on your last invoice?
Ramón: The email, yes; the address changed and it is now 12 Calle Mayor.
Assistant: Perfect, I will update your details, send you the link, and we will meet on Tuesday at ten.

words.note: A planned conversation between people for a purpose. Often used for any scheduled meeting.
A fixed time for a meeting. Often used with a professional or medical service.
A call over the internet with video. Common across Spanish-speaking countries.
Often shortened to correo or mail in conversation. Both are common.
Also means direction. Context shows the meaning.
A proof of payment for a purchase. Some regions also use it for a utility bill.
The regular account summary from a bank. Spain and some countries also say extracto de cuenta.
A paper or digital record a client must send or keep.
The place where a business works.
Confirmar una cita, un pago o un dato: to check and state that it is correct. It takes a direct object.

words.es: Le confirmo la cita del martes.
words.en: I am confirming your Tuesday appointment.
words.note: Use le for a client. Confirmar is often followed by the object: la cita, el pago, la reunión.

words.en: Can we hold the meeting by video call?

words.es: Envíe los documentos al correo de la oficina.
words.en: Send the documents to the office email.
words.note: Usted command. Regular -ar verbs end in -e: envíe; the accent on the i stays.

words.es: Traiga los recibos y el extracto bancario.
words.en: Bring the receipts and the bank statement.
words.note: Usted command of traer, for a meeting in person.
Le viene bien is a common polite phrase for convenience.

example.target: Confirmo la cita por correo.
example.native: I confirm the appointment by email.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The usted form confirma also means you confirm in a formal conversation, so context decides the subject.

example.target: Traigo los recibos a la reunión.
example.native: I bring the receipts to the meeting.

verbs.note: Irregular only in the yo form (traigo, with a g). Traes, trae, traemos and traen follow regular -er endings. Traer also gives the usted command traiga.

example.target: Envío la confirmación hoy mismo.
example.native: I will send the confirmation today.

verbs.note: The accent on envío, envías, envía and envían marks the stressed i. Enviamos has no accent because the stress falls on the e.

example.target: Llamo al cliente para confirmar.
example.native: I call the client to confirm.

verbs.note: A regular -ar verb. Llamar a means to call a person; llamar para means to call in order to.

passage.title: Documentos sobre el escritorio
target: Sebastián Ruiz revisa una pila de papeles en el escritorio del despacho.
Sebastián: Este documento es un estado de cuenta, no una factura.
Clara: ¿Y este papel es un recibo o un comprobante del pago?
Sebastián: Es un recibo del proveedor, con la fecha y el total pagado.
Clara: Estas facturas son de compras de la panadería, ¿verdad?
Sebastián: Sí; la factura pide un pago, y el recibo demuestra que el pago ya se hizo.
Clara: Entonces guardo las copias de los documentos y separo la declaración de impuestos del año pasado.
native: Sebastián Ruiz reviews a stack of papers on the office desk.
Sebastián: This document is a bank statement, not an invoice.
Clara: And is this paper a receipt or a proof of payment?
Sebastián: It is a receipt from the supplier, with the date and the total paid.
Clara: These invoices are for the bakery purchases, right?
Sebastián: Yes; the invoice requests a payment, and the receipt shows that the payment has already been made.
Clara: Then I keep copies of the documents and set aside last year's tax return.

words.note: The periodic summary from a bank or credit provider. The Spanish phrase estado de cuenta is widely used.
A bill that a seller issues to a buyer for goods or services. It states who sold, who bought, and the amount due.
A proof that money was paid. A receipt is not the same as an invoice.
A general term for a voucher or proof. In some countries it is used for a tax receipt or a payment slip.
A form that reports income or activity to a tax authority. The exact form depends on the jurisdiction.
A business that sells goods or services to your client. Plural proveedores.
A duplicate of an original document. Originals and copies are often filed separately.
The first version of a document, which may be needed for certification.
The date printed on a document. Check it before recording.
The final amount. Use total pagado for the amount paid.

words.es: Este documento es un estado de cuenta.
words.en: This document is a bank statement.

words.es: ¿Este papel es un recibo o una factura?
words.en: Is this paper a receipt or an invoice?
It is a receipt from the supplier.

words.es: Guardo las copias de los documentos.
words.en: I keep copies of the documents.
words.note: Guardo means I keep or store. Use with copias de when filing.

example.target: Identifico cada documento por su fecha.
example.native: I identify each document by its date.

verbs.note: A regular -ar verb with no spelling change in the yo form (identifico). Identificar takes a direct object and often pairs with por when naming a method.

example.target: Guardo las facturas en la carpeta.
example.native: I keep the invoices in the folder.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb with a direct object. Guardar means to store or keep something physically or digitally.

example.target: Separo los recibos por mes.
example.native: I sort the receipts by month.

verbs.note: Regular -ar. It takes a direct object and often pairs with por to show how items are grouped.

example.target: ¿Revisa usted el extracto con el recibo?
example.native: Do you check the statement against the receipt?

verbs.note: Revisa is the form for él, ella and usted. Revisar A con B means to check A against B.

passage.title: Revisión de un depósito
target: Marta y Julián revisan un depósito que llegó a la cuenta del negocio.
Marta: El monto es 1.250,50 euros, ¿correcto?
Julián: No, el extracto dice 1.205,50 euros en la misma fecha.
Marta: Repito la cifra del recibo: mil doscientos cincuenta euros con cincuenta céntimos.
Julián: Confirmo que la moneda es euro, no dólar, y que la cifra no coincide.
Marta: Anoto la diferencia de 45,00 euros en el registro.
Julián: Sumo el total otra vez y lo comparo con el extracto.
native: Marta and Julián review a deposit that reached the business account.
Marta: The amount is 1,250.50 euros, correct?
Julián: No, the statement says 1,205.50 euros on the same date.
Marta: I repeat the figure from the receipt: one thousand two hundred fifty euros and fifty cents.
Julián: I confirm that the currency is euro, not dollar, and that the figure does not match.
Marta: I note the 45.00-euro difference in the log.
Julián: I add the total again and compare it with the statement.

words.note: The sum of money in a transaction. Use in formal records and bank communications.
The money a transaction uses. Check it before recording any figure.
A number that represents an amount. Often used for a total or a balance.
The hundredth of a euro. In Latin America the word is centavo.
The gap between two numbers. Use for mismatched totals.
Money placed into an account. A deposit can also be a fee or security amount in some contexts.
A short name for the bank statement. Context makes it clear.
A written or digital entry. Use registrar to record a transaction.
The final sum of several amounts.
A bank account or a ledger account. Context shows which.

words.es: Confirmo que la moneda es euro.
words.en: I confirm that the currency is euro.
I repeat the figure on the receipt.

words.es: Anoto la diferencia en el registro.
words.en: I record the difference in the record.
words.note: Anotar means to write down or note; use it for short records.

example.target: Sumo las dos cifras antes de anotar.
example.native: I add the two figures before I note them.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Use sumar a for adding something to a total.

example.target: Repito el monto para confirmarlo.
example.native: I repeat the amount to confirm it.

verbs.note: Stem vowel change e to i in the yo, tú, él and ellos forms (repito, repites, repiten). Nosotros keeps the e: repetimos.

example.target: Anoto el monto en el registro.
example.native: I note the amount in the record.

verbs.note: Regular -ar. Anotar is for short written notes; registrar is for official entries.

example.target: Registramos el depósito hoy.
example.native: We record the deposit today.

verbs.note: Regular -ar. The yo form registro is also the noun registro, a record or log.

passage.title: Qué periodo cubre el extracto
target: Mónica pregunta qué periodo cubre el extracto que recibió el cliente.
Cliente: El documento cubre todo el año, ¿verdad?
Mónica: No, cubre desde el 1 de enero hasta el 31 de marzo de 2026, es decir, de enero a marzo.
Cliente: Entonces es solo el primer trimestre, no todo el año fiscal.
Mónica: Así es, y le envío hoy mismo el resumen del primer trimestre de 2026.
Cliente: ¿Cuál es la fecha de vencimiento para enviarle el resto?
Mónica: Nuestro plazo interno cierra el 10 de abril, así que conviene enviarlo esta semana.
native: Mónica asks which period the statement that the client received covers.
Client: The document covers the whole year, right?
Mónica: No, it covers from 1 January to 31 March 2026, that is, January to March.
Client: So it is only the first quarter, not the whole fiscal year.
Mónica: That's right, and I will send you the summary of the first quarter of 2026 today.
Client: What is the due date for sending you the rest?
Mónica: Our internal deadline closes on 10 April, so it is best to send it this week.

words.note: A span of time for a report. Período, with an accent, is also correct. Plural periodos.
A three-month period. Q1 is the first trimestre.
The twelve-month period a government or company uses for taxes and reporting. The months depend on the jurisdiction.
The day a transaction or document is dated. Use fecha de vencimiento for a due date.
The day a payment or filing must be made. Common in banking and tax notices.
A short report of results over a period.
A time limit for a task. Plazo is often used with a filing or payment.
Bank or account summary for a period.
A record or paper that shows information.
A calendar month. Plural meses.

words.en: Which period does this document cover?

words.es: Cubre desde el 1 de enero hasta el 31 de marzo.
words.en: It covers from 1 January to 31 March.

words.es: Le envío el resumen hoy mismo.
words.en: I will send you the summary today.
words.note: Spanish often uses the present for a near future action.

example.target: El resumen cubre todo el trimestre.
example.native: The summary covers the whole quarter.

verbs.note: Regular -ir verb with the stem cubr- in every form. In accounting, cubrir describes what a period, statement or policy includes.

example.target: La oficina cierra el trimestre el 10 de abril.
example.native: The office closes the quarter on 10 April.

verbs.note: Stem vowel change e to ie in the present (cierro). The nosotros form keeps the e: cerramos.

example.target: El extracto indica la fecha de corte.
example.native: The statement indicates the cut-off date.

verbs.note: Regular -ar. Indicar takes a direct object (the fecha); in a formal letter the verb is common for stating a requirement.

passage.title: Ingresos y gastos del mes
target: Lorena quiere saber cuánto ganó la panadería el mes pasado.
Dueña: Los ingresos fueron de 3.200 euros por las ventas del mercado.
Lorena: ¿Y qué gastos pagó el negocio?
Dueña: Pagué la harina y la luz, en total gasté 1.150 euros.
Lorena: Entonces la ganancia fue de 2.050 euros, ¿verdad?
Dueña: Sí, pero una cafetería todavía no pagó la factura de la semana pasada.
Lorena: Anoto ese cobro como pendiente y mañana lo confirmo con la cafetería.
native: Lorena wants to know how much the bakery earned last month.
Owner: The income was 3,200 euros from market sales.
Lorena: And what expenses did the business pay?
Owner: I paid for the flour and the electricity, in total I spent 1,150 euros.
Lorena: So the profit was 2,050 euros, right?
Owner: Yes, but a café has not yet paid last week's invoice.
Lorena: I note that collection as pending, and tomorrow I will confirm it with the café.

words.note: Money a business receives from sales or services. Plural ingresos.
Money a business pays out. Gastos is plural.
A transaction in which goods or services are sold.
A business that sells goods or services to yours.
Money paid to settle a bill or a debt.
A payment or task that is not finished yet. Pendiente is an adjective; it agrees with the noun.
Use pasado after the month to say last month. Useful in financial conversations.
What remains after expenses are subtracted from income. Not the same as cash in the bank.
The moment or act of receiving money owed to you.
A number used for an amount, a total or a balance.

words.en: How much did the bakery earn this month?
What expenses did the business pay?
words.note: Pagó is preterite of pagar, the completed action.

words.es: Ganó más de lo que gastó.
words.en: It earned more than it spent.

words.note: Queda is a common way to ask what remains.

words.es: Los ingresos suben y los gastos bajan.

example.target: La panadería gana dinero con el mercado.
example.native: The bakery earns money from the market.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The preterite form ganó refers to a finished amount, such as last month's total.

example.target: Gasto poco en electricidad.
example.native: I spend little on electricity.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. In the preterite, gasté (I spent) and gastó (he or she spent) stress the last syllable.

example.target: Pago la factura cada mes.
example.native: I pay the invoice every month.

verbs.note: Regular in the present. Before e it adds u to keep the hard g: pagué, pague. Pagar takes the bill as object and the payee with a.

example.target: Cobramos la venta cuando el cliente paga.
example.native: We collect the sale when the client pays.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. In business it means to collect money owed or charge a fee, which is different from pagar.

passage.title: El saldo no es lo que puedo gastar
target: Julia es nueva en el despacho y revisa el estado de cuenta del cliente.
Mario: El saldo de la cuenta corriente es de 2.400 euros.
Julia: ¿Y todo ese saldo está disponible para pagar hoy?
Mario: No, hay un cargo pendiente de 600 euros que el banco ya retuvo, pero todavía no ha liquidado.
Julia: Entonces el saldo disponible es de 1.800 euros, y tenemos menos fondos de lo que parece.
Mario: Exacto: el saldo no es negativo, pero el dinero disponible es más bajo.
Julia: Anoto el saldo contable y el saldo disponible por separado, junto con el cargo pendiente.
native: Julia is new at the office and reviews the client's account statement.
Mario: The current account balance is 2,400 euros.
Julia: And is all that balance available to pay today?
Mario: No, there is a pending 600-euro charge that the bank has already put on hold but has not yet settled.
Julia: So the available balance is 1,800 euros, and we have fewer funds than it seems.
Mario: Exactly: the balance is not negative, but the money available is lower.
Julia: I note the book balance and the available balance separately, along with the pending charge.

words.note: The amount in an account at a given moment. Saldo contable is the book balance; saldo disponible is what can be used now.
Money that can be used now. Disponible agrees with the noun it describes.
A bank account for daily payments. Term used in Spain and many Latin American countries.
Money placed into an account.
Money taken out of an account. Retirar means to take money out.
An amount taken from an account.
An amount added to an account.
Periodic summary from the bank.
A charge by a bank or an agent. Check whether a fee applies.
Money held or available for a purpose.

words.es: ¿Cuál es el saldo de la cuenta?
words.en: What is the balance of the account?

words.es: El saldo disponible es menor que el saldo contable.
words.en: The available balance is smaller than the book balance.
We have enough funds to pay.

words.es: Hay una comisión por el retiro.
words.en: There is a fee for the withdrawal.

example.target: Tenemos suficiente dinero para pagar.
example.native: We have enough money to pay.

verbs.note: Irregular: tengo has a g, and tienes, tiene and tienen change e to ie. Nosotros keeps the e: tenemos.

example.target: Queda un saldo de 200 euros.
example.native: A balance of 200 euros remains.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Quedar means to remain; use it for what is left after a payment or deduction.

example.target: Depositamos el cheque hoy.
example.native: We deposit the check today.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The noun depósito is the matching word; depositar takes the amount as direct object.

example.target: Retiro el efectivo del banco.
example.native: I withdraw the cash from the bank.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. The noun retiro is the matching word. Use retirar with an amount or cash, not with a payment.

passage.title: Debe, haber y tarjetas
target: Patricia enseña a Rubén cómo leer un asiento en el libro mayor.
Patricia: El debe está a la izquierda y el haber a la derecha.
Rubén: ¿Entonces débito y crédito son lo mismo que la tarjeta de débito?
Patricia: No, en la contabilidad son columnas; la tarjeta es un medio de pago.
Rubén: Y la tarjeta de crédito, ¿es un préstamo del banco?
Patricia: En la práctica sí: el banco presta dinero hasta el límite y el titular debe devolver lo gastado.
Rubén: Entonces cada compra tiene un débito en una cuenta y un crédito en otra, aunque se pague con tarjeta.
Patricia: Exacto; una compra con tarjeta de crédito va al debe de gastos y al haber de la deuda con la tarjeta.
native: Patricia shows Rubén how to read an entry in the ledger.
Patricia: The debit side is on the left and the credit side on the right.
Rubén: So debit and credit are the same as the debit card?
Patricia: No, in bookkeeping they are columns; the card is a means of payment.
Rubén: And the credit card, is it a loan from the bank?
Patricia: In practice, yes: the bank lends money up to the limit, and the cardholder must pay back what was spent.
Rubén: So every purchase has a debit in one account and a credit in another, even when it is paid by card.
Patricia: Exactly; a credit card purchase goes on the debit side of expenses and the credit side of the card liability.

words.note: The left column of a ledger entry where amounts are recorded as debits.
The right column of a ledger entry. Haber is also an infinitive meaning to have.
Latin America: débito/crédito for entries. Spain: cargo/abono or debe/haber. Débito also names debit-card payments.
A bookkeeping entry, a credit card or a loan. Context decides.
A card that lets the holder borrow up to a limit and pay later.
A card that takes money directly from the linked account.
Money borrowed under agreed terms and repaid with interest.
A record in the ledger showing debit and credit amounts for one transaction.
The book or system that holds all account records.
The maximum amount allowed. Useful for credit cards.

words.es: El debe está a la izquierda.
words.en: The debit side is on the left.

words.es: ¿Esto es un débito o un crédito?
words.en: Is this a debit or a credit?

words.es: La tarjeta de crédito tiene un límite.
words.en: The credit card has a limit.

words.es: Debe pagar el préstamo cada mes.
words.en: He or she must make a loan payment each month.

example.target: Debo revisar el asiento antes de cerrar.
example.native: I must review the entry before closing.

verbs.note: Regular -er verb. Use deber with an infinitive for obligation; the same verb without an infinitive means to owe.

example.target: El banco carga la comisión a la cuenta.
example.native: The bank charges the fee to the account.

verbs.note: Regular in the present. Before e it adds u: cargué, cargue. Cargar a una cuenta means to debit that account or to charge a fee to it.

example.target: Abonamos el pago en la cuenta del cliente.
example.native: We credit the payment to the client's account.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Abonar a means to credit an account. In a formal setting abonar can also mean to pay an amount.

example.target: Uso la tarjeta solo para compras del negocio.
example.native: I use the card only for business purchases.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Usar is a common verb for a card or a service; it has no stem change.

passage.title: Documento que falta
target: Ana Lucía llama a un cliente porque no recibió el recibo de la compra de marzo.
Ana Lucía: Buenos días, me hace falta el recibo de la compra de marzo.
Cliente: Lo tengo en papel, pero no lo he escaneado todavía.
Ana Lucía: ¿Podría enviármelo por el canal que acordamos, por favor?
Cliente: Sí, lo envío esta tarde. ¿Para qué fecha lo necesita?
Ana Lucía: Lo necesito antes del viernes para cerrar el mes de marzo.
Cliente: Perfecto, en el mismo correo incluyo el número de factura y el extracto del banco.
native: Ana Lucía calls a client because she did not receive the purchase receipt from March.
Ana Lucía: Good morning, I am missing the March purchase receipt.
Client: I have it on paper, but I have not scanned it yet.
Ana Lucía: Could you send it to me through the channel we agreed, please?
Client: Yes, I will send it this afternoon. By what date do you need it?
Ana Lucía: I need it before Friday to close the month of March.
Client: Perfect, in the same email I will include the invoice number and the bank statement.

words.note: A proof of a payment. Ask for the original if the copy is unclear.
Any paper or file the client gives.
A document that confirms who the person is. Often requested before a bank change.
Short for correo electrónico. Use the address the client agreed.
The day or time by which the document is needed.
The method of contact agreed by both sides, such as email or a secure portal.
A regular summary from a bank or card.
A bill for goods or services.
A formal request. Pedido usually means a purchase order.
The person or method used to reach someone.

words.es: ¿Podría enviarme el recibo de la compra?
words.en: Could you send me the purchase receipt?

words.es: Me hace falta el extracto de marzo.
words.en: I am missing the March statement.

words.es: Por favor, envíelo por el canal acordado.
words.en: Please send it through the agreed channel.
By which date do you need it?

example.target: Pido el recibo por escrito.
example.native: I ask for the receipt in writing.

verbs.note: Stem change e to i in the yo, tú, él and ellos forms (pido, pides, piden). Nosotros keeps the e: pedimos.

example.target: Le recuerdo el plazo de entrega.
example.native: I remind you of the delivery deadline.

verbs.note: Stem change o to ue in the yo, tú, él and ellos forms (recuerdo). Nosotros keeps the o: recordamos. Le recuerdo means I remind you.

example.target: Espero el documento antes del viernes.
example.native: I expect the document before Friday.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb. Esperar can mean to wait for or to expect, which the context must make clear.

example.target: Incluyo el extracto con el correo.
example.native: I include the statement with the email.

verbs.note: Incluir adds y before the ending in the yo, tú, él and ellos forms: incluyo, incluyes, incluye, incluyen. Nosotros is regular: incluimos.

passage.title: Cierre de la llamada
target: Gabriela cierra una llamada rutinaria con un cliente sobre documentos de abril.
Gabriela: Hoy recibí el extracto del banco y el resumen de ventas.
Cliente: ¿Y qué falta todavía?
Gabriela: Queda pendiente el recibo de la compra de la harina.
Cliente: Lo envío mañana por la mañana, ¿le sirve?
Gabriela: Sí, quedamos en revisar todo el jueves a las diez.
Cliente: Perfecto, ¿me manda la confirmación por correo?
Gabriela: Claro, le envío el resumen y la fecha de la próxima cita hoy mismo.
native: Gabriela ends a routine call with a client about April documents.
Gabriela: Today I received the bank statement and the sales summary.
Client: And what is still missing?
Gabriela: The receipt for the flour purchase is still outstanding.
Client: I will send it tomorrow morning; does that work for you?
Gabriela: Yes, we agreed to review everything on Thursday at ten.
Client: Perfect, will you send the confirmation by email?
Gabriela: Of course, I will send you the summary and the date of the next appointment today.

words.note: Verb form for receiving a document or payment.
Fixed meeting time for the next review.
An item that still needs action.
Bank summary already received.
A short report of the exchange or of the results.
A decision both sides accept.
The day of the next appointment.
The full set of records for a task.
Action to check progress after a meeting.
Written or spoken proof that a date or request was accepted.

words.es: Quedamos en revisar todo el jueves.
words.en: We agreed to review everything on Thursday.

words.es: Queda pendiente el recibo de marzo.
words.en: The March receipt is still outstanding.

words.es: Le envío el resumen por correo hoy.
words.en: I will send you the summary by email today.
words.note: Spanish often uses the present for a near-future action; English uses will.

words.es: Nos vemos la próxima semana para el seguimiento.
words.en: We will meet next week for the follow-up.

words.es: ¿Le parece bien el jueves a las diez?
words.en: Does Thursday at ten suit you?

example.target: Recibo el extracto cada mes.
example.native: I receive the statement every month.

verbs.note: Regular -ir verb in the present tense: recibo, recibes, recibe, recibimos, reciben. The preterite recibí is the completed form.

example.target: Quedamos en la próxima cita.
example.native: We agreed on the next appointment.

verbs.note: Quedar en means to agree on, and quedar plus a participle means to be left in a state.

example.target: Le agradezco el envío del resumen.
example.native: I thank you for sending the summary.

verbs.note: Only the yo form is irregular (agradezco). The other forms are regular: agradeces, agradece, agradecemos, agradecen.

example.target: Acordamos la fecha por correo.
example.native: We agree on the date by email.

verbs.note: Stem change o to ue in every present form except nosotros: acuerdo, acuerdas, acuerdan; acordamos. Acordarse de means to remember.
